page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2a server family. It is powered by an ARM-based Ampere Altra processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance features 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates that the t2a-standard-2 delivers modest performance across various workloads. In single-core CPU testing, the stress-ng benchmark recorded a score of 1812.29, placing it in the average tier, while its multi-core score of 3594.57 falls into the weak category. Memory performance is constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 26.99 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 16.42 GB/sec. Passmark testing highlights limitations in complex operations, yielding a CPU score of 1596.29 and a memory score of 858.29, both categorized as poor. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware-accelerated AES, though the Passmark encryption test remains low at 321.71.

Due to its ARM architecture and resource density, the t2a-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient profile for entry-level workloads that do not require x86 compatibility or high-performance computing. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and simple database operations, as evidenced by its passmark database score of 1416.76. However, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive applications, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, where its small-model prompt processing speed is limited to 86.25 tokens per second.
